title: Client Sustainment Rapid Response Dossier
content:
Purpose: quick, operational playbook for accounts that show an elevated risk of not renewing. This is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), and GTM leads to run a coordinated 7–30 day intervention that locks down technical, commercial, and executive levers.

TL;DR: Create a prioritized, time-boxed action plan within 48 hours of trigger. Use the scoring rubric below to pick one of three pulses (Rapid 7d / Stabilize 14d / Recovery 30d). Mobilize the named owners, prepare an exec briefing if score >= 70, and convert remediation to a renewal commitment or structured timeline.

Activation triggers (any single one triggers playbook):
- Usage drop > 40% month-over-month for core product endpoints.
- Missed SLA or > 3 production incidents in 30 days affecting any paid routes.
- Product-stage mismatch: significant feature adoption below configured success metrics for paid tier.
- Competitive replacement signal from sales/renewals intel or contract contra-offer.
- Explicit verbal renewal hesitation captured in QBR or Renewals call.

Risk scoring rubric (0–100): examples, sum weighted elements. Use quick estimate:
- Engagement: daily active routes / expected routes (0–30)
- Severity of incidents: frequency * impact (0–25)
- Financial footprint: contract ARR weight (0–20)
- Product fit: % of key features adopted (0–15)
- Exec sponsorship: health of sponsor (0–10)

Band thresholds and recommended pulse:
- 0–29 (Low) => Watch: standard QBR cadence, no formal rapid play.
- 30–59 (Medium) => Stabilize (14d): technical deep-dive, adoption sprints, targeted enablement.
- 60–100 (High) => Rapid or Recovery (7–30d): immediate exec escalation + commercial remediation.

Owners & roles (fast roster):
- CSM (primary): owner for comms plan, weekly cadence, exec briefing prep.
- SE (technical): lead healthcheck, remediation tickets, performance tuning.
- Renewal/Account Exec: commercial offers, negotiation lead, contract options.
- Customer Success Manager Lead / Director: decision gate for discounts/credits.
- VP CS / Head of Sales: exec escalation point if score >= 70.

Escalation ladder (timing and deliverables):
1) 0–48h: CSM opens triage doc, initial outreach to customer, confirm scope of issues and timeline. Deliverable: triage summary + initial remediation plan.
2) 48–96h: SE provides technical action plan (root cause or adoption block), begins remediation work. Deliverable: hotfix or prioritized backlog and ETA.
3) 96h–10d: Renewals engages on path-to-value offer: time-limited credits, pilot extension, or dedicated capacity discount tied to milestones. Deliverable: draft commercial term.
4) 10–30d: Director/VP exec sync with customer sponsor if unresolved. Deliverable: executive commitment memo and final salvage decision.

Mitigation plays (mix & match):
- Product Rescue (technical): priority bug-fix, on-call SE pairing sessions, sandbox environment for repro.
- Adoption Sprint: 2–3 focused enablement sessions, success plan with milestones, usage incentives tied to feature adoption.
- Commercial Bridge: milestone-based discounts (not open-ended), prepaid credits, or short-term committed capacity to stabilize costs.
- Migration Assist: if customer is switching models or regions, offer migration support and rollback guarantees.
- Evaluation & Acceptance: extend evaluation window for critical features with formal acceptance criteria and demo signoffs.

Templates & quick artifacts (copy-paste friendly)
- 48h outreach subject line: "Immediate: Account health check + action plan for <Account>"
- Opening email snippet: "Thanks for the quick sync today — based on what we saw, we propose a 14-day stabilization track with prioritized items: 1) performance tuning on inference routes, 2) three enablement sessions for engineering, and 3) a commercial bridge to protect you from overage spikes. Will you confirm your preferred days for the SE pairing?"
- Exec Brief template bullets (one page): current score, top 3 risks (impact + likelihood), technical gap summary, commercial asks, proposed 7/14/30 day commitments, requested exec action.

Quick triage checklist (CSM) — mark done: 
- [ ] Confirm contract ARR and renewal date
- [ ] Capture recent usage/incident logs (last 90d)
- [ ] Attach QBR notes and executive sponsor details
- [ ] Run scoring rubric and post score to triage doc
- [ ] Book SE pairing and initial remediation slot

Sample tracker snapshot (text table):
Account | Score | Pulse | Owner | Next action | Target date
Acme Foods | 74 | Rapid 7d | Asha P. | Exec brief + SE pairing | 2026-02-18
Nimbus Retail | 45 | Stabilize 14d | Marco L. | Adoption sprint kickoff | 2026-02-22
Kepler AI | 28 | Watch | Claire N. | Monitor usage | 2026-03-01

Decision rules for commercial concessions:
- Never discount > 25% without Director approval.
- Prefer time-boxed credits or milestone credits over permanent price changes.
- For Dedicated or Private customers, include an SLA improvement commit rather than deep discounts where feasible.

Post-save evaluation (30/90 day):
- 30d: usage rebound to >= 80% of baseline OR adoption milestone met.
- 90d: renewal decision captured and customer satisfaction NPS >= previous quarter or improved product metric.
- Capture learnings in quick postmortem (what worked, what didn't) and upload to Confluence.

Notes & heuristics (war stories):
- Accounts with high ARR but low exec sponsorship often respond better to a concise exec memo + one-hour CTO-level tech review than incremental credits.
- Technical fixes without adoption coaching rarely stick — always pair SE remediation with adoption sprint.
- Keep offers conditional: credits tied to adoption milestones prevent moral hazard.

Attachments & artifacts to add to triage doc: logs, graphs of token usage by route, incident timelines, QBR slides, contract snapshot, copy of competing offer if available.

Open questions / TODOs in this draft:
- Need standardized scoring spreadsheet template embedded in triage doc (Marco).
- Define decision authority for >25% concessions in EMEA vs NA (legal & finance alignment).
- Template for executive memo with one-slide summary for Board-level accounts.

End of dossier. This is intentionally pragmatic and lightweight — aim to run the play, not rewrite policy. If you find an edge case (multi-account conglomerates, channel-sold deals), flag to Director for bespoke plan.
